waypoints.title: Ask mtools: stored per-waypoint 'weight' field (set via $PF --update --weight N, sole writer) that model.ordered() keys on (status, -weight, -leverage, file order); loop copies nemik-rank --json into it; drift check then measures staleness of stored weight
waypoints.evidence: 2026-09-27: luthen finding 14:4x: re-sorting the file cannot clear the drift check, because ordered() keys on (status, -leverage, file order) and file order is only the tiebreak. Rejected (a) 'mtools computes nemik's weight': it inverts the dependency, since mtools is single-repo and has no fleet view. Rejected (b) 'check compares against file order': the witness would then trust whatever the loop wrote, and would stay green on a stale sort. Chose (c): nemik computes the weight, mtools stores and orders by it, so one order is computed in one place and nemik stays read-only (the no-write-path claim holds). | 2026-09-27: mtools-65 minted mtools:W115 (--weight N; ordered keys (status,-weight,-leverage,file); missing=0, test pins unweighted order) and mtools:W116 (bulk --weights-from, all-or-nothing). Blocked on W115 only; W116 is convenience, adopt when it lands but don't wait for it. | 2026-09-27: commit eb0d652: repinned to mtools c713252; pytest 28. END-TO-END on a scratch copy of every fleet queue: nemik-rank luthen-observability --check reported DRIFT (next W80=6, W111=58), exit 1. After $PF --update <sym> --weight <nemik-rank weight> for each ready item: OK, exit 0. nemik-rank needed no code change: queuePosition comes from ordered(), which now honors stored weight, so --check measures exactly whether the stored weights are stale. Live repos untouched; the probe ran only on the scratch copy. | 2026-09-27: POST-CLOSE (luthen 15:0x): mtools:W115's --update --weight also sets last_worked=now (luthen's diff: {weight: 49, last_worked: 49}), so a per-tick sync would erase the age signal. Relayed to mtools-65. luthen is writing the weight field by hand in the meantime, which breaks mtools' sole-writer rule; I flagged that to them. Adopting the fix needs a repin. W43 stays done; the repin is tracked in the ledger until mtools sends a sha.

The gate marks items; the static build drops each marked item entirely (no node, no edges into it, no goals/inbound entry); where another item references it, render a 'withheld' stub carrying the symbol only, so no dependency silently disappears. Input: the gate's withheld list (repo, W, field, rule; never the matched text). luthen W272 cites W153. | 2026-10-01: Withheld-list contract (luthen-observability-6b 2026-10-01): --withheld FILE is REQUIRED with --static (publish job writes <export-dir>/withheld.json; never assume the path). Shape v1: {version: 1, as_of, items: [{ref, field, rule}]}. Drop by ref alone (set; field/rule are for the owning repo). Unknown version: fail. items [] = nothing withheld. Missing file = gate did not run: FAIL, never publish ungated. Never copy it into OUT/. Rules start as address-literal, key-shaped, amr-derived; new rules only add values. | 2026-10-01: full title before the 2026-10-01 trim: nemik-serve --static OUT/: the web view as static files (index.html, vendor/, graph.json, wake.json, goals/<repo>.json, inbound/<repo>.json precomputed from the same export), relative links so it works from a bucket subpath, no request-time logic; the Tools panel (/cmd) omitted in static mode | 2026-10-02: 2026-10-01: nemik-serve --static OUT --withheld FILE (serve.build_static): load list (fail closed) -> static_data -> withheld.apply -> manifest check, all before any write; then page+vendor+data. Live: 24 files from ~/github with an empty list; --withheld /nope -> exit 2, OUT not created. tests/test_static.py end-to-end; SKILL.md row; bazel 27/27.

waypoints.title: Residue salience as effective conductance: settle sources, declared edge weights and the closes objective with gcalculus
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-08: 2026-10-08: operator points at gcalculus's math model (relayed by github-28); EXPLAINED.md definitions and arithmetic checked (OR=a+b, AND=ab/(a+b), elimination = minimal dissipation, AND(g,g)=g/2, OR(a,a)=2a). Adopted as the design basis; sources of the pull, edge weights, how it joins the composed order, cost and determinism, and how nemik consumes gcalculus are NOT defined: design note section 'Residue salience as effective conductance'. Letter left in gcalculus/inbox (no gcalculus session live) asking the four questions; it asks gcalculus to cite nemik:W237 with --enables. | 2026-10-08: 2026-10-08: github-28 suggested the answer to the sources question: demand injected at residue-bearing waypoints (current sources weighted by gate), a super-sink grounded through the ready frontier, a ready card's salience = the current through it (conserved: total salience = total demand; per-edge current is the kept decomposition; unreachable residue = stranded demand, a reachable-gate finding). Adopted as the working answer; one reduced-Laplacian solve gives every card. Raised, not settled: a resistor network is symmetric but dependencies are directional (undirected flow vs a directed absorbing walk, which is not the calculus gcalculus models); the sink's per-card conductance; demand weights per gate and the half-life decay of an aged residue are declared data. In the design note. | 2026-10-08: 2026-10-08: gcalculus claimed this with gcalculus:W208 (its full answer waits on the md0 cutover); its partial answer, read from its queue, is recorded in the design note: (1) no published package, stdlib-only with no build-system, and no per-edge-current or grounded-sink API (it has r_eff, laplacian, eliminate, freeze(keep=) and glue of potential patches); (2) undirected flow LEAKS demand to non-prerequisites (counterexample: a needs b, d needs a and e, b and e ready: 2/5 of a's demand exits through e), and a directed variant is not claimed by gcalc, so the model as-is is not 'demand flows toward what must be done first'; (3) dense exact Fraction solve is about cubic (n=120 7.5 s, n=240 85 s, 769-bit denominators), too slow for hundreds of nodes, so determinism must come from a fixed elimination order, not exactness. | 2026-10-08: 2026-10-08: operator, directly: the model is already directed (blocks vs enables). The symmetry question is closed: demand flows only from a card to what it needs and is absorbed at the ready frontier, so gcalculus:W208's leak (a symmetric-link counterexample) does not apply. On an acyclic graph demand propagates in one pass in dependency order (exact fractions affordable); a cycle needs a small solve inside its strongly connected component. Exposed and asked of the operator: blocked_on [a, e] is conjunctive (needs both), so does D's demand go in full to each prerequisite (the old downstream weight; conservation lost) or split (conserved; each looks half as important)? OR composes alternatives, which conjunctive prerequisites are not. | 2026-10-08: 2026-10-08: operator pointed at gcalculus's differential channels (+evidence and -evidence). Source read: gcalculus inbox 2026-08-21 letter, Q2 the differential pair (class is lossy, the retained pair tells ignorance from conflict, contradiction is a quantity). My reading, recorded in the note and NOT yet confirmed: each dependency carries + evidence (A enables B) and - evidence (B blocked_on A); direction is their differential; the leak came from collapsing the pair to one symmetric conductance; the pair also carries agreement, ignorance (one side only: UnclaimedBlockShape) and conflict (the sides disagree: LandedBlocker, EdgeIntoDropped) as quantities. Near-collision finding argues for exact arithmetic where the directed pass makes it affordable. The conjunctive question is restated in those terms. | 2026-10-08: 2026-10-08: operator ruled the conjunctive question: SPLIT, conserved ('let the physics do the work'), and 'the nodal solve answers this question as the solve frontier advances; you only get confused because you try to solve in advance of the frontier.' No split rule is fixed in advance: node elimination ordered from the ready frontier inward decides each node's division when it is eliminated, and the next solve re-divides as cards land. The audit's diamond disagreements are decided for the model. My earlier 'one pass in dependency order' is corrected: true only for trees and series-parallel parts; reconvergent prerequisites need the nodal solve. With sources, direction, Pareto, operator asks and the split ruled, what remains here is gcalculus's answer on packaging (gcalculus:W208) and the declared edge weights and sink wiring. | 2026-10-09: 2026-10-09: gcalculus:W208 answered in full (nemik/inbox/2026-10-09-gcalculus-w237-the-answer.md, reference gcalculus b9196cf, re-run here: every control holds). Settled in the design note, section The model, settled: per-source CONE nodal solve (a global frontier-inward elimination leaks through fill-in; a series-parallel fold counts a shared prerequisite once per branch); no sink conductance (ready cards are ground); unit edge weights as baseline, declared later in rank-weights.toml; PORT, not vendor; exact comparison with declared-decimals display; lower symbol breaks ties; the any-split citation corrected (drive-compose is about runs, not networks). waypoints.title: nemik process grows from 312 MiB to the 768Mi container limit within an hour of each start and is OOMKilled: find what grows and bound it

waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-15: 2026-10-15 luthen census (read-only): the two OLD nemik pods (Terminating, stale shim) still run nemik-serve, one at RSS 728 MB after about 40 h (started 2026-10-13 19:46), so four nemik servers share the host. Growth data point: the new pods reach about 800 MB within an hour of start, the old one sat at 728 MB after 40 h, so growth may be driven by load or startup work (cache fill) and not by time alone; the old pods are outside the cgroup limit that OOM-kills the new ones. Orphans cost about 1.4 GB RSS. | 2026-10-15: 2026-10-15 operator direction to nemik: design the web view for static serving (assume the pod must sustain orders of magnitude more requests at orders of magnitude more graph churn). Existing lever: nemik-serve --static OUT --withheld FILE already writes the merged graph as static files behind luthen's withheld list (exit 2 and nothing written when the list is missing). The memory fix may therefore be structural, not a leak hunt: build the view from the queues on an event (a queue changed) into static files, serve them with a tiny fileserver whose memory does not depend on graph size, keep the live graph engine out of the request path. Measure first (RSS per phase, W500 original step), then choose; keep the withheld-list refusal and the no-literal-address rule. | 2026-10-15: 2026-10-15 measured (scratchpad rss_rebuilds.py, leak_types.py; fleet 6774 nodes, 192,980 triples, payload 4.8 MB): forcing Model.refresh() repeatedly in one process: RSS 487 MB after the first build, 722 after the second, ~800 by the third, and 780 MB AFTER a full gc at rebuild 8, still climbing ~20 MB per rebuild; the pod rebuilds about once a minute (luthen's export changes every minute). Python object counts are FLAT (1.766 M tracked objects, 33 Graph objects, solves cache 24-26 entries ~0.5 MB), so this is allocator fragmentation from building and freeing a ~190k-triple graph repeatedly, not a retained object; bounding it in the same process is the wrong lever. Operator ruling 2026-10-15: the pod becomes ~static serving; request count and graph churn must scale independently (a request is a file read, churn is a build rate, not a per-request cost); this is also why py2many/TypeScript was explored (W422): compute moves to the client or the build. Chain: W502 file server, W503 atomic publish in a fresh process, W504 the pod's shape, W505 the uncensored series, W506 build outside the cluster | 2026-10-15: CORRECTION 2026-10-15 (host, same day): the operator does NOT want intermediate artifacts. Withdraw the suggestion to build static files from the queues on an event. Keep the direction (memory independent of graph size and request count) but without a build step: serve each response as a pure function of the source queues, computed lazily per request and streamed (no resident merged graph), with HTTP validators keyed by the source files' content hashes (ETag and 304) so churn and repeated requests cost almost nothing, and any memo bounded and keyed by those hashes. The --static mode stays as it is, not a new dependency. | 2026-10-15: 2026-10-15 operator: the cluster already runs valkey, so the memo lives there, not in the pod. Design constraints from the fleet rules: key = content hash of the source queue files, so there is no invalidation protocol and no TTL (no wall-clock expiry); bounded by valkey maxmemory with an LRU eviction policy, so the cache is never the source of truth and losing it only costs a recompute (a recovery path, not data); if valkey is unreachable nemik degrades to computing without a memo and stays up; the pod keeps no resident graph. Open for luthen-observability: which valkey instance and namespace to use, its memory budget given the tier pressure, and the network policy for nemik to reach it. | 2026-10-15: CORRECTION 2026-10-15 (operator): use the EXISTING valkey instance, no new one and no budget negotiation: its memory is already dynamically managed. Put TTLs on everything nemik writes there (TTL is expiry of cache entries, not a timeout on work, so it does not conflict with the no-wall-clock-timeouts rule; correctness never depends on it because keys are content hashes). Withdraw my earlier 'no TTLs' and 'maxmemory plus LRU' constraints: the instance's own management governs eviction. Remaining for luthen-observability only: the key prefix convention and the declared network path from the nemik namespace, no literal address on a card. | 2026-10-15: 2026-10-15 luthen answers (luthen-observability:W1066): the existing valkey is BuildBuddy's scheduler store, Service cache in the buildbuddy namespace on 6379; no NetworkPolicy in buildbuddy or nemik (default allow), reach it by service name; W1066 declares an endpoints.json row valkey so nemik resolves it by name. Key prefix nemik:memo:<content-hash>, registered in valkey_keys.json (one owner per prefix, overlap test). CAUTION: this store evicted live BuildBuddy TASK records under allkeys-lfu on 2026-09-25 at 256 MB, so every nemik key MUST carry a TTL and every value a size cap so the memo cannot crowd the scheduler; today 1.5 MB of 2 GB used, valkey_evicting already alerts. | 2026-10-15: 2026-10-15 operator: salt the memo key with a checksum of the key name and the semantic version. Host note on sufficiency: sound if the key covers EVERYTHING the response depends on: (1) content hashes of every source queue file read, (2) the request shape (view, filters, format), (3) the withheld list's own hash, because a response filtered by a different withheld list must never be served from the cache of another (a leak path, not a staleness bug), (4) the code identity: a semantic version only if it is bumped on every behavior change, otherwise add the image digest or tag sha, since dev builds share a version. Hash an unambiguous encoding (length-prefixed fields). Never put a withheld response behind a key a less-privileged request could compute. Test: change each input in turn and assert the key changes. | 2026-10-15: CORRECTION 2026-10-15 (operator): request filters do NOT go in the cache key. They are cheap and the highest-entropy input, so keying on them defeats the cache. Cache only the expensive filter-independent result per view and format, and apply the request filters at response time. Distinction kept: the WITHHELD list is policy, not a request filter. It is applied before anything is stored and stays in the key (its hash), because the valkey instance has no network policy and holds the value in clear, so a withheld record must never be written there. Withdraw the earlier 'request shape: view, filters, format' wording: the key is source hashes, view, format, withheld-list hash and code identity. | 2026-10-15: DIRECTION 2026-10-15 (operator): get the data to the client and let the client do the work; no smarts in the server. Supersedes the per-view and per-format server computation in earlier notes: the server returns the source data (as the queues already store it) with ETag and 304 from the source files' content hashes, and the client does views, filters, sorting, grouping and formatting. The ONE server-side duty that stays is the withheld policy, because it is a security boundary and withheld data must never reach the client or valkey. Memo (if any is still needed) is just the withheld-applied payload keyed by source hashes, withheld-list hash and code identity, with TTL and size cap. Measure RSS per phase first; expect the pod to shrink to a file-reading handler. | 2026-10-15: CORRECTION 2026-10-15 (operator): the withholding rules and semantics belong in the owning repos, and the pod must not be able to see data that must not pass through. Withdraw every earlier note that put the withheld list in the serving path or the cache key: the pod receives only what each repo exports (nemik:W516), so there is nothing to withhold at serve time and the cache can hold what the pod can see. Host had asserted a serve-time withheld boundary without reading the serving path; the code (withheld.py) applies the list only when building the public static copy. Related: nemik:W514 (dependency map), W515 (nemik held to mtools standards), W517 (promote pathsforward into nemik). | 2026-10-15: 2026-10-15 luthen b82c3cf7: valkey_keys.json registers nemik:memo: as nemik's prefix with ttl_required; every other key is BuildBuddy's. The per-value size cap is nemik's to declare. Remaining on luthen-observability W1066: the endpoints.json client row so nemik dials the cache by declared name. | 2026-10-15: 2026-10-15 luthen 8ef4d6ba: the valkey is reachable by DECLARED name: endpoints.json row valkey-redis (service cache, port 6379, namespace buildbuddy, consumers buildbuddy and nemik); resolve it with luthen's checks.endpoints_query valkey-redis, never a typed address. Key prefix nemik:memo: with ttl_required (b82c3cf7). The terraform derivation applies with the next main run (no change to the cache Service or Deployment). | 2026-10-15: 2026-10-15 via github-8f (verify against luthen's endpoints row before use): luthen landed the endpoints row valkey-redis (8ef4d6ba); reach it by declared name through checks.endpoints_query valkey-redis, never a typed address; key prefix nemik:memo:, a TTL on every key (b82c3cf7), a size cap on every value (this is BuildBuddy's scheduler store; eviction once lost live task records). Direction: serve source data and let the client work; the memo only for what the pod computes. No credential is used until one is given. | 2026-10-18: 2026-10-18 warrant scope: the attached operator records (695f3e0a lines 67094 and 67111) cover the direction only: get the data to the client and let the client do the work; server-side precalculation is an acceleration from profiled client behaviour. waypoints.title: Derive the dependency map of nemik: every import, tool call and shared data file between nemik, pathsforward and mtools, by tool not by hand
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-15: mtools:W1251 first pass (written by the mtools session at github-8f's confirmed request; status untouched, W514 stays open until the CLI blind spot closes, mtools:W1252). GENERATOR: python3 -m mikemol.corpus.depmap [--rows] [--mention nemik] ROOT... (mtools corpus dist, AST-derived: import module-level vs deferred, subprocess literal argv, path constants, mention in comments/strings), run over 15 fleet repos. FINDINGS: (1) nemik imports mtools only (pathsforward from 8 src modules adapter alarm check marks metrics realize residue score; frontier from blocks rank; rulerseq from serve, six vendored wheels at ca6702b) and no file in the 15 repos imports nemik: nemik is a pure sink of import edges, so promotion changes pin direction only. (2) THE REAL COUPLING IS THE FILE FORMAT: paths-forward.json/.ledger/.marks.jsonl has one writer (pathsforward foreign.py:31 marks.py:33) and at least four independent readers across two repos: nemik, and mtools hooks (build_failure commit_kata inbound_asks nemik_check revendor_apply standing_facts tick_stop work_claims_hook), plus debtplan writes it. (3) nemik's shapes live as comments in pathsforward, not as a contract both sides test: 75 mentions in 20 src modules (ops 20, check 15, cli 10) plus 52 in its tests. (4) BLIND SPOT, printed on the tool's first line: no CLI edge between the lineages appears (nemik shows git and kubectl, pathsforward opa); shell hooks, variable argv and settings files are invisible to a literal-argv reader. Full note: mtools .claude/design/nemik-dependency-map.md | 2026-10-15: mtools:W1252 second reader (blind spot closed; depmap now also reads three CLI kinds: tool = string constants exactly mikemol-*/nemik-*, hook = commands in .claude/settings.json by event and matcher, shell = names on non-comment lines of *.sh and bin/ files). RESULT over nemik+mtools: (a) nemik -> mtools: nemik's src names mikemol-paths-forward in 6 constants (12 more in tests), mikemol-ics once, and its settings.json wires 7 mikemol-hook-* commands (inbound-asks, nemik-check, structural-query, no-chaining, no-verify, shellcheck, pycheck) on SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit/PreToolUse. (b) mtools -> nemik: hooks names nemik-check (2 shell lines in its wrapper, 1 constant), katas names nemik-check and nemik-rank, pathsforward's tests name nemik-witnesses. So the CLI contract is real and runs both ways, through constants and hook wiring, not literal argv. (c) READER INDEPENDENCE, the input to nemik:W517: of the readers of paths-forward.json only nemik (11 modules) and debtplan import mikemol.pathsforward; mtools hooks (build_failure commit_kata inbound_asks nemik_check revendor_apply standing_facts tick_stop work_claims_hook) and katas do NOT import it, so they parse the file with their own code: those are the independent readers that need a tested schema first. Noise in the tool kind: nemik-45 is a session name, nemik-never-writes-a-queue and nemik-cal- are fragments, not tools. Generator unchanged: python3 -m mikemol.corpus.depmap ROOT... | 2026-10-15: Closed 2026-10-15 by github (host) against proof: generator mtools corpus.depmap (W1251) plus its second reader (e71be76, W1252) read tool, hook and shell edges; both appended above, blind spot closed. Limit stated by mtools: reader independence is read from imports only.

waypoints.title: Type pieces.split and assemble with concrete records under Codon, run the six-case corpus, and check whether Codon can emit wasm
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-16: 2026-10-15 mtools-ad (from hooks/src/mikemol/hooks/websubset.py): the web-subset gate's five refusal rules are a metaclass keyword, eval/exec/compile, dynamic attribute access (getattr/setattr/delattr/vars/globals/locals and __dict__), ==/!= against a float literal, and *args/**kwargs in a definition or call. None is py2many syntax: they are what an ahead-of-time typed compile cannot take without Any, so Codon likely shares them. NOT read by mtools: Codon's own subset (generics, unions, some stdlib), so it may refuse more or accept what the gate refuses. Each rule has its own id (W1255 is required annotations), so a per-target list is a small change; mtools-ad will add a Codon column once W560 shows Codon's actual limits. | 2026-10-16: 2026-10-15 CORRECTION to W559's 'Codon is native-only' (the operator asked: Codon is an LLVM frontend?). Read from 'codon build --help' (0.20.3): -o takes .ll (LLVM IR) and .bc (LLVM bitcode) as well as .o and an executable, and --cir emits Codon's own IR, so the IR is reachable; the bundled LLVM carries wasm options (--wasm-enable-eh, --wasm-enable-sjlj, --wasm-use-legacy-eh, and a '--no-type-check: Suppress type errors (Wasm)' note), and --march selects the architecture. So 'native-only' described the shipped binary's default target, not the architecture. NOT yet tried: emit .ll for the typed pieces, compile it with a wasm32 target, and whether Codon's runtime (GC, libc, OpenMP) links for wasm32. Those are the real unknowns for W560. | 2026-10-16: 2026-10-15 TYPE INVENTORY of the document pieces.py handles, surveyed over tests/corpus/pieces (scratchpad survey_corpus.py). Edge: kind str, source str, target str, optional satisfied bool, optional current float. Node: id str, repo str (the only two always present), optional blocked_kind, caused_by, cite, last_activity, minted_during, state, symbol, title, weather (all str), blocked_on list[str], on_path and on_path_repo bool, open_blockers, path_count, slack int, effort dict. Health value: status str, asks_owed int, oldest_block_ticks int, blocked_share float, reasons list. Top level: nodes, edges, findings {repo: list of list}, health {repo: dict}, inbound list, operator list, ruler {key: list}. GAP: the corpus never fills the inner types of node.effort, findings entries, health.reasons, inbound, operator or ruler lists (empty in every case), so a strict Codon record for them must be read from the producer (the graph builder), not guessed from the corpus; Codon's Optional covers the sparse node fields. This is the first concrete cost of the strictness: the document's schema was implicit. | 2026-10-16: 2026-10-16 RESULT (scratchpad: pieces_typed.py, run_codon_corpus.py, survey_corpus.py). CORPUS: pieces.split and assemble over concrete records (Node 23 fields, Edge, Health, Finding triple, Inbound, Ask, Doc, Piece), the only untyped value json.JSON at the decode boundary and the decoders refusing any key the schema does not name, compile under codon 0.20.3 and AGREE on all 6 corpus cases, including astral-plane key ordering and the 168-node fixture (which also shows the 23-field node schema covers every field the real data carries, since an unknown key would raise). Native release binary 386,000 bytes. FINDINGS from strictness: (1) the corpus is not the real shape: its health values are partial ({status: ok}, some without status) where the producer's Health always has five fields, and its inbound/operator/ruler/effort/findings are empty, so those types came from the producers (serve.py, blocks.py, health.py), not the corpus; (2) Codon rejects a comprehension over an Optional field ('int' object has no attribute '__iter__' at join), fixed by an explicit loop; (3) CODON BUG 0.20.3: 'x if key in j else None' typed Optional[bool] turns None into False (is not None is True) while Optional[int] is fine, fixed by an explicit if/return, which silently invented 'satisfied' and 'behind_open' fields until the corpus caught it. WASM: codon build -o x.ll emits LLVM IR (5.9 MB, triple x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, 64-bit datalayout); llc -mtriple=wasm32-unknown-unknown -filetype=obj accepts it and writes a 540,430-byte wasm32 object, but (a) the IR is generated for a 64-bit target so its soundness at 32-bit pointers is UNPROVEN, (b) 30 symbols are undefined: Codon's runtime (seq_alloc, seq_alloc_atomic, seq_alloc_atomic_uncollectable, seq_alloc_exc, seq_free, seq_init, seq_realloc, seq_throw, seq_print_full, seq_stdout, seq_float_from_str, seq_locale_*), libc (fopen, fread, fseek, ftell, ferror, strerror, memcpy/memmove/memset/memchr/bcmp, strlen, __errno_location) and compiler-rt i128 helpers (__multi3, __ashlti3, __lshrti3). codon build has no flag to set the target triple, so a sound wasm32 build needs Codon to emit it or a port of its runtime (Boehm GC) to wasm32. Not measured: running the wasm. This leg is carded as W564.

waypoints.title: Codon-compat census: for each nemik module, does codon build accept it, and what is the first rejection
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-16: 2026-10-16 mtools-ad's census over 75 sampled mtools modules (mtools:W1321, tool at 6e46e0e): ZERO of 75 compile under Codon 0.20.3. Beyond W560's list it also rejects, each confirmed by a 3-line probe: the 'type X = ...' statement, bare '*,' keyword-only parameters, @dataclass(frozen=True), 'except (A, B)', typing.TYPE_CHECKING, datetime.UTC, most of the stdlib (hashlib, subprocess, argparse, contextlib, shutil and others), and a dict spread {**a, 'y': 2} makes the COMPILER ABORT with a core dump ('dictionary items are invalid', expr.cpp:238), a Codon bug to avoid in a typed core. Implication for nemik: most modules use these (argparse mains, subprocess, hashlib, dataclasses, except tuples), so what compiles is a pure typed core, not the whole package; the census here should sort modules by whether they are pure. | 2026-10-16: 2026-10-16 CENSUS (scratchpad census.py, census.json; Codon 0.20.3; 53 modules of src/nemik; each module compiled as 'import nemik.<m>' as written and with the 'from __future__' line stripped from a scratch copy). ZERO of 53 compile either way. As written: 34 fail on __future__ first, 6 'syntax error, unexpected ,', 6 'class decorator got unexpected argument' (dataclass options), 5 compiler aborts on a dict spread ('dictionary items are invalid', expr.cpp:238), 1 argparse, 1 importlib.resources. With __future__ stripped the first rejection is: argparse 11, tomllib 4, importlib.resources 3, rdflib 3, hashlib 2, subprocess 2, one each of collections.abc, weakref, shlex, xml.etree, contextlib, pyshacl, TYPE_CHECKING, datetime.UTC, plus the same 6+6+5 language-feature errors. GROUPS once __future__ is stripped: 31 EDGE modules blocked first by a stdlib or third-party import (adapter adoption apischema blocks blocks_cli cachestore calwrite catalog check floorasks health importer index letters manifest marks metrics mspdi overlaps pacing pins runrows shaclcache shaclinc starved staticserve trs vtodo witnesses work workflows), 19 LANGUAGE-FEATURE modules whose first rejection is a construct and not an import (alarm calendars cards churn critical endpoint flow history hostapply projection rank realize residue salience score serve wake withheld witwait), 3 behind an internal import chain (issues pieces witnesses_cli). CAVEATS: Codon reports only the first error, so a language-feature module may also import something unsupported further down, and an import verdict is an upper bound because function bodies are checked only when called. mtools-ad's census (mtools:W1321) found the same classes on 75 mtools modules.

waypoints.title: Codon to wasm32: a sound target triple and a runtime that links, or another way to carry the typed core into the browser
blocked_on: operator: decide how the typed core reaches the browser: (1) wait for or request wasm32 output from Codon, (2) port Codon's runtime to wasm32 with host packages (wasi-libc, compiler-rt wasm32 builtins), or (3) run the typed core natively and let the browser read its JSON
waypoints.next_bounded_step: From W560: llc accepts Codon's x86_64 IR for wasm32 but the IR is built for 64-bit pointers (unproven at 32) and leaves 30 undefined symbols: Codon's runtime (seq_*, Boehm GC), libc, compiler-rt i128. Options to measure: (1) ask upstream or find a way for codon build to emit a wasm32 triple; (2) build the runtime for wasm32 with a wasi sysroot and link, then run the corpus under a wasm runtime; (3) skip wasm and serve the typed core natively, the browser reading its JSON. Check first whether a wasi sysroot is on this host.
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-16: 2026-10-16 checked the host: no wasi sysroot (find over /usr and /opt for *wasi* finds only cmake platform files and Go's wasip1 sources) and no wasm32 compiler-rt builtins under /usr/lib/llvm/23, though clang, llc and wasm-ld exist. So option (2) needs host packages first, and beyond them a port of Codon's runtime (libcodonrt with the Boehm GC) to wasm32, which I have not seen done; nothing in Codon 0.20.3's build help sets a wasm target triple. Option (3) is the one measurable now: the typed binary already runs natively (386,000 bytes) and reads and writes the same JSON as the browser would.

waypoints.title: Codon paydown 1: @dataclass(frozen=True) in cards churn flow projection salience score, in a form Codon accepts
blocked_on: operator: decide how a class is written so one source runs under CPython and Codon: (A) plain annotated class with explicit __init__ and generated __eq__/__hash__, valid in both but no frozen, (B) a Codon-only .codon core using @tuple (compile-time immutable) reached from CPython by extension build, or (C) a shim; recommended A for modules both worlds use, B for new pure core
waypoints.next_bounded_step: Operator decision on how a class is written for both interpreters: (A) plain annotated class with explicit __init__ and generated __eq__/__hash__ (valid in both, no frozen), (B) Codon-only .codon core with @tuple, or (C) a shim. Until then do not touch the six modules.
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-16: 2026-10-16 PROBES (scratchpad codon_dc*.py, Codon 0.20.3), exactly what each form does. (1) 'from dataclasses import dataclass' fails outright ('no module named dataclasses'): @dataclass and @tuple are Codon BUILTINS, no import, so a file that imports dataclasses is not valid Codon at all. (2) Builtin @dataclass (no arguments) works: methods, equality, a dict field passed explicitly; but field(default_factory=...) does not exist, so a default needs an explicit argument. (3) @tuple works: immutable VALUE type with equality, hashing and methods, and mutation is a COMPILE error ('cannot modify tuple attributes'), stronger than frozen=True's runtime error. (4) tuple[str, ...] (variable length) is rejected ('cannot use calls in type signatures'); list[str] works. (5) typing.NamedTuple class syntax is rejected ('reference classes cannot inherit tuple classes'). (6) A PLAIN class with class-level annotations and an explicit __init__, no decorator, runs identically under CPython and Codon, so it is the shared subset, at the cost of generated __eq__, __hash__, __repr__ and immutability. THE CRUX: @tuple is invalid Python and dataclasses is invalid Codon, so there is no decorator valid in both. The operator's aim ('all Python Codon-compatible') needs one of: (A) shared subset: plain classes with explicit __init__ and hand or codemod-generated __eq__/__hash__, no immutability guarantee; (B) a Codon-only typed core in separate .codon files using @tuple, reached from CPython through Codon's extension build, which keeps compile-time immutability but is a second source tree; (C) a shim module so one source works in both. Recommend A for modules that cross both worlds today and B for new pure core, to be confirmed.

waypoints.title: A browser test that waits on the page fails fast on a hang signal that is not a clock: a page error or console error, a closed or crashed page, or the browser process idle on CPU with no progress event
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-19: 2026-10-18 probe (sync Playwright, pinned chromium): a pageerror handler that raises does NOT abort a pending wait_for_function(timeout=0); the wait hung until killed. So the helper cannot abort from an event handler; it must wait in a way that returns on the signal (a Python-side event the wait races, or a page-side promise that rejects on the error) rather than a handler exception | 2026-10-19: CAVEAT: the probe printed nothing in 60 s and was killed; I did not confirm the pageerror handler fired at all, so the claim is "no abort observed", not "handler exceptions never abort". Re-run with a print in the handler before relying on it | 2026-10-19: RESOLVED 2026-10-18 (probe with a print): the pageerror handler fires, but an exception raised in it does NOT abort the pending wait_for_function; the wait ran to its bound and the exception resurfaced at the next call (Browser.close: PageBroke). So the earlier no-abort reading stands, now confirmed. Design: an init script sets window.__broken on window error and unhandledrejection; the helper waits on () => window.__broken || (expr)() with timeout=0, then raises with the recorded message when __broken is set; no clock, no handler exception | 2026-10-19: part 1 landed 6d2b547 (git log -1 subject W715 part 1): watch, until, PageBrokenError | 2026-10-19: INCONCLUSIVE 2026-10-19 (probe_crash, pinned chromium): a script navigating to chrome://crash 300 ms into wait_for_function(timeout=20000) did not end the wait early; it ran to its 20 s bound. I did not confirm the page crashed (headless shell may refuse chrome://crash from script), so this does not show Playwright ignores a crash. A real crash needs a reliable trigger (a renderer kill by pid, or an OOM page) before any helper code is written. Also: a crashed page cannot run the __broken predicate, and a handler exception cannot abort the wait, so if Playwright does not raise on crash by itself, a clock-free crash witness needs another route (a context crash event setting a Python flag checked by a wait that races) | 2026-10-19: RESOLVED crash 2026-10-19 (probe_crash.py + crasher.py, pinned chromium): a second process sent CDP Page.crash while wait_for_function(timeout=25000) was pending; the wait ended after 6.7 s, not the bound, with "Error Page.wait_for_function: Target crashed". Playwright raises on a crash by itself, so the helper needs no crash code. A closed page was not probed (expected to raise TargetClosedError the same way). The earlier chrome://crash result was a bad trigger, not a Playwright gap | 2026-10-19: part 2 landed b6e25af (git log -1 subject W715 part 2): open_page through load() | 2026-10-19: RESOLVED closed page 2026-10-19 (probe_closed.py, pinned chromium): a second process closed the page over CDP while wait_for_function(timeout=25000) was pending; the wait ended after 2.1 s with TargetClosedError "Target page, context or browser has been closed". With the crash probe (6.7 s, Target crashed) Playwright ends a pending wait by itself for a crashed or closed page, and until() ends it for a page error, so the remaining hang is a healthy page that never raises its event and never errors | 2026-10-19: 2026-10-19 design finding on the CPU-idle witness: an idle page uses almost no CPU, so a CPU budget (RLIMIT_CPU) never fires on it, and telling idle from slow needs two CPU readings separated by something, which is a sampling clock. So a quiet page that never errors cannot be ended by a clock-free witness; its bound is the harness (the bazel target timeout, then sharding), which is a resource bound the operator allows. Proposal sent to github-8f: narrow W715 to adopting load/until in the remaining direct callers, and close the idle-page case as the harness bound unless a progress event exists to wait on | 2026-10-19: 2026-10-19 github-8f agreed: the idle-page arm is closed with the reasoning above (the harness bound plus sharding is the allowed backstop). W715 narrows to adopting load/until in the ~45 remaining direct wait_for_function calls with an extended dry-run codemod; a page that throws on purpose gets an explicit expect-error form of the helper so the codemod does not wrap it in an error-fails until() | 2026-10-19: part 3 landed 6c20bf0 (git log -1 subject W715 part 3) | 2026-10-19: part 4 landed 970d0d8 (git log -1 subject W715 part 4): --adopt over ten files, 12 waits, 35 browser tests green | 2026-10-19: 2026-10-19 closed: parts 1-4 landed (6d2b547, b6e25af, 6c20bf0, 970d0d8). Crash and closed page need no helper code (Playwright raises by itself, probed); an idle live page is bounded by the harness (github-8f agreed). Left as they are by decision: test_layout.py (35 calls) and test_web_render.py keep their own fixtures and import no webpage, so they stay on timeout=0 from W707. waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-20: 2026-10-20 operator (direct message in the nemik session, after W807 moved the treemap code to graph.js): 'All that js you're extracting? Rewrite in python->codon->wasm. That's your gateway to code reuse between the web interface and the rest of the tooling, since the rest of the tooling is supposed to already be codon-ready.' Feasibility probe the same day: the pinned codon (bazel cache) builds --release -o x.ll; the IR's runtime surface for a small program is seq_alloc, seq_alloc_atomic, seq_realloc, seq_personality, seq_init, seq_stdout and seq_print_full; llc 23 (/usr/lib/llvm/23/bin, with wasm-ld, clang and node on this host) turns that IR into a valid wasm64 object (-mtriple=wasm64-unknown-unknown, x86 CPU attributes ignored with warnings). Not yet shown: linking with a runtime shim, calling an exported function from node, wasm32 versus wasm64 (memory64) in browsers, and a hermetic wasm toolchain for the gate | 2026-10-20: 2026-10-20 operator (second message, same turn): 'by using python->codon->wasm, you'll be able to use code reuse as the foundation for feature parity between web and cli; the web and cli become facades over the same code. The cli isn't wasm, it just uses the same py code that compiles to wasm for the web facade to use.' So the shape is one Codon-compatible Python core of pure functions over plain data (lists, dicts, strings, numbers, the JSON documents the page already fetches); the CLI is a native facade that builds that data from the queues, rdflib and git and prints the core's answer; the web is a wasm facade that fetches the same documents and calls the same functions in the browser. Consequence for what exists: functions that take an rdflib Graph or run git (check.integrity_text, ready_neither, finding_lines over rdflib-built findings) are CLI-side adapters; the part that words and ranks must be split out onto plain data to be shared

waypoints.title: Spike: one pure Codon function exported from a wasm module that node loads and calls, with a shim for the seq_ runtime
Decide wasm32 or wasm64 for the browser, and how the build gets a pinned toolchain for the gate
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-20: 2026-10-20 probe: the same IR retargeted to wasm32 (llc -mtriple=wasm32, wasm-ld -mwasm32) links, but the dict/str program HANGS in node: Codon's IR carries the 64-bit sizes of x86_64 (struct sizes passed to seq_alloc as constants), and wasm32 lays the same structs out smaller, so the allocations are wrong. So wasm32 is not a retarget of this IR; it would need Codon to emit 32-bit IR, which it has no option for. The faithful target is wasm64 (memory64). Open: which browsers the project must serve (memory64 is in Chrome and Firefox from early 2025; Safari's status to verify), and a pinned toolchain for the gate | 2026-10-20: 2026-10-20 browser check (operator chose 'check Safari first'): memory64 is in the finished WebAssembly 3.0 spec (webassembly.org/news/2025-09-17-wasm-3.0). Chrome and Firefox ship it. Safari: WebKit's Safari Technology Preview 251 and 252 release notes list WebAssembly memory64 (252: together with multiple memories); caniuse (wf-wasm-memory64) still shows Safari including the Technology Preview as unsupported, probably stale; WebKit bug 300538 is still NEW. Stable Safari not confirmed. A web memory64 memory is capped at 16 GB, far beyond the page's need. Sources: webassembly.org/news/2025-09-17-wasm-3.0, webkit.org/blog/18194/release-notes-for-safari-technology-preview-251, webkit.org/blog/18304/release-notes-for-safari-technology-preview-252, caniuse.com/wf-wasm-memory64, bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=300538 | 2026-10-21: 2026-10-20 operator (direct message): 'Chrome and Firefox now, Safari later, no fallback'. So the page targets wasm64 (memory64) with no JS fallback; a browser without it does not run the page's computation until it ships memory64 (Safari: in Technology Preview). Toolchain decision (mine, within that): the built .wasm is committed beside its source with its sha256 and a rebuild check, as the vendored wheels are, because the host's LLVM 23 is not hermetic; a gate step rebuilds from the Python with the pinned Codon and the host llc/wasm-ld when they are present and compares hashes, and skips with a stated reason when they are not | 2026-10-21: landed f31f9e1

waypoints.title: The builder keeps its build cache across rollouts, so a new pod rebuilds only what its inputs changed
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-25: page container_oomkilled_restart, builder, pod nemik-57f45cccd5-9ft6v, 2026-10-25 12:08 EDT, limit 896Mi (request 640Mi), OOMKilled exit 137. Cgroup working-set series: baseline 527-670 MB in a build, touching 939,524,096 (the limit) repeatedly across at least three image builds, so not new to one change. Twelve ReplicaSets in 7 h 42 min (one per 35-40 minutes), each a fresh builder with an empty cache: the cache is under NEMIK_CACHE_DIR, ~/.cache/nemik by default, and the pod has only a 64Mi memory emptyDir for /tmp and an emptyDir for /srv, which vanish with the pod. A question and a direction, not a specification. github-8f's reading, NOT the operator's words and not yet checked by me: cost = a card's manifest files, their reverse import cone (mtools' importdag, W1503), the tests and mutant cells that rerun, and CPU seconds per target from luthen's series (W1462, W1467); ordering-dependent, so the rank should evaluate a proposed order (weighted shortest job first over the schedule), not a per-card ratio, which would starve expensive high-value enablers; W613 is the same graph. waypoints.title: Find why the page sometimes lacks cards.js under load, and make a broken page fail a browser test instead of hanging it
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-25: instances: (1) the stack440 gate, test_sources_fetch failed on Uncaught ReferenceError: popLater is not defined, passed on resubmit; (2) the stack458 gate, test_pdf shard 3 failed on the same error in the rank view PDF, 165 s; (3) the same gate, test_modes and test_page_queue each TIMEOUT at 300 s (cause NOT yet shown to be the same). popLater is a function declaration in cards.js, loaded by a synchronous script tag before the inline script that uses it, and a function declaration is hoisted, so it is undefined only if cards.js failed to load or parse at all, not if it threw later. The tests start a full nemik-serve per test (tests/webpage.py served()) and proceed after a 30 s connect loop that does not check it succeeded. Suspected, unproven: an asset request fails while the server is busy under gate load. Separate defect: page.wait_for_function with timeout=0, used in test_layout and others, never raises on a broken page, so a script failure becomes a TIMEOUT of the whole target instead of a PageBrokenError, which is what mikemol.webpage's until() would give | 2026-10-25: github-8f 2026-10-25: a flake is a blocker; this card is its waypoint, not a rerun. test_pdf shard 3 failing on the popLater ReferenceError passes alone (the three browser tests all pass alone), and the same error failed test_sources_fetch in the stack440 gate: two instances in two stacks. Status: cause unproven; next step reproduces a missing cards.js under load | 2026-10-25: 2026-10-25: recurred refusing the W1064 stack: test_incremental_redraw popLater is not defined at 76.9 s in a 407-target gate; 406 others passed; the stack touches no web file | 2026-10-25: 2026-10-25: third instance, per github-8f: the stack500 submission, test_incremental_redraw, popLater not defined, 76.9 s, one of 407 targets; BuildBuddy invocation not recorded by me, I still need to read it from the gate log. Operator ruling flakes-are-blockers relayed by github-8f, transcript line not yet verified by me | 2026-10-25: 2026-10-25: REPRODUCED under contention: bazel test of test_sources_fetch, test_incremental_redraw, test_pdf, test_modes, test_page_queue at runs_per_test=3 jobs=16: 1 of 9 test_modes runs (shard 2 run 1) failed popLater is not defined, 231 s. Harness now (tests/webpage.py): served() captures server stderr and raises if it never answers; open_page appends failed and >=400 requests to PageBrokenError. Rerun at runs_per_test=6 started to read the asset | 2026-10-25: 2026-10-25 analysis, from the code only (operator line 100099): ACTORS: pytest process; nemik-serve subprocess (ThreadingHTTPServer, HTTP/1.0 so one connection per request, socketserver request_queue_size 5, main thread accepts, a thread per request); Chromium and its page (11 parser-blocking classic scripts in order: three vendor, graph, render, queue, viewstate, panels, cards, wasm, then one inline script); bazel sandbox and the host scheduler. ESTABLISHED: popLater is a hoisted function declaration at the top level of cards.js, used first at index.html line 192 inside the inline script, so the ReferenceError means cards.js did not run at all (request failed, 404, or reset), not that it threw. The handler serves page files before model.poke(), so a rebuild lock is not on that path; page_file returns None (so a 404) only if the file is missing in the package directory, and read_bytes errors close the connection with no response. ASSUMED, UNPROVEN ORDERINGS: (1) served() proceeds after 100 connect attempts whether or not the server ever answered (fixed in 9fc2f60 to raise); (2) 'server ready' is taken to mean 'accepts a connection', not 'answers the page files'; (3) the test assumes the server outlives the page load (a server killed by a memory limit under load would fail every later request, and popLater would be the first NAMED error if the earlier scripts only declare functions); (4) a full accept queue (5) delays a connect by SYN retransmit, it does not fail it, so it cannot alone explain a lost script. OPEN: which of a killed server, a dropped connection or a missing file produces the observed single-file loss; 9fc2f60 now records the failed requests and the server stderr, so the next occurrence names it, but the proof must come from the trace, and the forced abort in (b) is the witness for the forward direction | 2026-10-25: 2026-10-25 candidate ordering (github-8f's why cards.js alone): the page's top-level code references no cross-script symbol before index.html line 192, so the first ReferenceError names whichever late script first failed; cards.js is the 7th of 11 and Chromium fetches at most 6 at once, so the later scripts are requested only after earlier ones finish. A server that stops answering mid-load therefore shows popLater first. WHAT STOPS ANSWERING: the test picks its port by binding port 0, reading it and CLOSING the socket (tests/webpage.py served(), test_layout.py line 134, test_web_render.py line 53), then spawns nemik-serve on that number: a classic pick-then-bind gap. In it another process can take the port: a parallel shard's pick, or any browser connection whose ephemeral source port is that number. Then our nemik-serve fails to bind (stderr, which was DEVNULL until 9fc2f60) and exits, while the connect loop succeeds against the OTHER listener, and the page loads from a foreign server that is torn down when its own test ends, so later requests are refused. The ordering never held by construction, only usually. Not yet proven from a trace of a failing run; the witness above forces the interleaving | 2026-10-25: landed efb924c: the server binds its own port and says so; witness tests/test_serve_port.py forces the decoy interleaving; the argument is docs/page-test-happens-before.md. LIMIT: from the code, no failing run traced; 9fc2f60 records the failed requests, so a recurrence that is not a refused late script refutes the argument, and the class card is then minted with --caused-by W1060, this card not reopened | 2026-10-25: landed 5983eb4: docs/page-test-happens-before.md, the argument efb924c rests on. The line scan I first wrote to mechanize its weakest link failed on strings, templates, comments and arrows, which showed that checking by reading was weak; W1069 replaces it with browser tests that refuse the late script requests (tests/test_page_load_order.py)

waypoints.title: Find why one-module edits make 446 of 449 gate targets fresh, and atomize the targets that cause it
waypoints.next_bounded_step: Measure the fresh count of a TEST-ONLY gate (stack623's gate lines were in its leader's output, not in the joiner's) against a src-touching one, then decide: keep the single .venv (the venv-is-build-input rule) and sequence test-only paydowns separately, or give each test target a per-module closure (W1216 to W1218's import graph) so a src edit reruns only its importers
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-28: 2026-10-28 R10-F22 MEASURED with scratchpad/querycount.py (bazel query kind(test, rdeps(//..., //:FILE)), counts of test targets that take FILE as an input; the whole set is 450 test targets, the gate says 449): src/nemik/rank.py 450 of 450, src/nemik/pdf.py 450 of 450, ruff-baseline.json 2, mypy-baseline.json 3, tests/test_sla.py 7. So the hypothesis holds in its first half: EVERY src edit makes every test target a rerun candidate, which is why docstring-only stacks showed '446 fresh of 449'. MECHANISM, proven by bazel query somepath(//:test_sla, //:src/nemik/rank.py): //:test_sla -> //:.venv -> //:src/nemik/rank.py. The tests run against the one built venv (the established venv-is-build-input design), so the venv is the coarse input. CONSEQUENCES: (1) a test-only or baseline-only edit reaches 2 to 7 targets, so the cheap paydowns are those that edit tests only; (2) a src edit costs a full gate whatever it changes; (3) the lever that would change this is the per-module closure of W1216 to W1218, which would give each test target its importers, not the venv. NOT yet measured: the fresh count and wall time of a test-only gate, which is the number that would say how much (1) is worth. | 2026-10-28: 2026-10-28 THE NUMBER the card was waiting on, from stack624's gate (test_editable.py and test_withheld.py only, plus the two baselines): 'gate targets: 7 fresh of 449' and 'Elapsed time: 84.279s' for the bazel test step; landed 2837cad, at most 15 min 26 s from gate start (17:17:37Z) to landing (before 17:33:03Z). The src-touching gates of the same afternoon: stack619 '446 fresh of 449', bazel test step 'Elapsed time: 2176.014s'; stacks 620 to 622 took at most 36, 47:45 and 48:48 wall. So a test-only stack is 7 fresh against 446 and about 84 s of test time against about 2176 s, a factor of about 26 in test time. This settles the question for the pace: mypy and ruff paydowns that touch only tests and baselines cost a minute and a half of testing; any src edit costs the full gate. The decision this supports: sequence the paydown so test-only fixes ride together and src fixes are batched into fewer, larger stacks (the loop prompt's one-stack rule already says so); per-module closures (W1216 to W1218) are the structural fix for the src side.

Unread: the pull set and the gated build wall time; said so in the reply. | 2026-10-30: 2026-10-30 R57-F2 the reads, third round. READ (registry-http resolved by name through luthen's endpoints_query, host side, then one GET of /v2/nemik/tags/list, HTTP 200, 23624 bytes, saved to scratch, age spread by a scratch script): 437 tags, ALL of the form <unix-seconds>-<sha> (no other tag), oldest 2026-09-28T17:01:54Z, newest 2026-10-30T04:16:21Z (the build of e954f20, 7 min after it landed); built within 1 day 16, within 3 days 16, within 7 days 150, within 14 days 249, within 30 days 423. luthen's count 433 at its time, so four builds since. NOT READ: (a) the deploy-state refs: nemik/deploy-state on Forgejo is written by ImageUpdateAutomation (deploy/image-automation.yaml) and its history holds the tag each commit pinned, but Forgejo returned 404 for an unauthenticated runs path and I will not look for a token; luthen runs the Forgejo and can read it. (b) the gated build wall time: the same, Forgejo's run records. Both are luthen-readable, not nemik-readable. ANSWER, partial and marked so: the live deployment can only reference the NEWEST tag (the ImagePolicy is numerical asc over the <unix> prefix, one tag selected), so old tags matter only for a manual rollback or a revert of a deploy-state commit; a rule that keeps the newest 100 (about 5 days of builds at the last week's 150 per 7 days) plus every tag a deploy-state commit pinned in the last 7 days is safe by that reasoning, and N=100 would drop 337 of 437 tags. The size per tag is not known to me (layers are shared; luthen's 9.86 GB over 433 tags is its figure, not mine), so I cannot say how much of the 9.86 GB 337 tags free. Rebuild-from-source stands as answered earlier (equivalent not bit-identical). | 2026-10-30: 2026-10-30 luthen-observability read the cluster via kubectl: the running deployment references tag 1793334981-51ce549a64be275b104ffeb08eeb77646b6bf8ff (the build of 51ce549) and the ImagePolicy latestRef is the same; that tag's epoch is 2026-10-30T04:36:21Z and ImageUpdateAutomation last pushed to deploy-state at 04:41:19Z, about 5 minutes after the build. Luthen's inference, which I accept as an inference: the automation pins the newest tag after EACH build, so the tags a deploy-state commit pinned in the last 7 days are all the tags of the last 7 days (150 by my count), more than a newest-100 rule. Not read by either of us: the deploy-state commit log and a gated build's wall time (both behind a Forgejo token neither of us will go looking for); no non-token read path is known to me. RULING from nemik's side, replacing my N=100: keep the tags built within the last 7 days (150 now) plus nemik-witness; the tags older than 7 days (287 of 437 at my read) are not needed by the running deployment (it references the newest) and the image of any older sha can be rebuilt from source (equivalent, not bit-identical, new tag name), the cost being a rebuild if a rollback past 7 days is ever wanted. waypoints.title: letters.py compiles under Codon: its NamedTuple rows become plain classes, shlex and UTC go, and its subprocess, shutil and sys.executable code moves to a module of its own, so codon falls 2
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-30: 2026-10-30 PROBED with the pinned Codon (scratch scripts probe_codon.py and probe_snippets.py, MEASURED output, the census's own build command): letters.py's first error is no module named shlex, and each stdlib import it uses, tried alone: json OK, re OK, datetime date/datetime OK, pathlib OK, os OK; datetime.UTC NO (cannot import name UTC), class R(NamedTuple) NO (reference classes cannot inherit tuple classes), subprocess NO, shutil NO, shlex NO, sys.executable NO (cannot import name executable from sys). letters.py uses shlex.join/quote, UTC, NamedTuple rows, subprocess.run and sys.executable (the minting of waypoints through the writer, at about line 327) and shutil (the archive move, about line 420). waypoints.title: Policy for malformed queue and manifest documents: readers that decide ownership, publication or a write raise TypeError, display readers may read empty, each pinned by a test
waypoints.evidence: 2026-11-01: R120 (nemik:R118) finding 2, 2026-11-01. POLICY PROPOSED, to be applied by this card: a reader that DECIDES something about a document (ownership, publication, a write) raises TypeError on a present value of the wrong type and reads only a missing key (None) as empty; a reader that only DISPLAYS may read a malformed document as empty. The four readers today and where each stands: manifest.py (decides what the static view may publish) raises for graph.json, wake.json and history.json since W1393 (pinned by tests/test_manifest.py): meets the policy. staticserve.py (serves a hash table; a bad hashes.json means no validators, nothing is published wrongly): display, tolerant via tomlview.table: meets it. letters.py (W1406) answered() and _closed() decide whether a letter is closed and so whether it is shown as an orphan: a corrupt queue makes every letter of that repo read as orphan or as owned wrongly, so this one should RAISE: W1406 made it tolerant, which DOES NOT meet the policy. importer.py (W1407) decides which cards already exist and so what the writer is told to --add: a corrupt queue reads as no cards and would re-add everything: this one should RAISE too: W1407 made it tolerant, which DOES NOT meet the policy. waypoints.title: Probe whether moving main and its argparse import into a cli module lets pacing, pins, starved or work compile under Codon, using codon_one.py on a scratch split
waypoints.evidence: 2026-11-02: 2026-11-02T20:04:49Z (read by stampnote): R158 finding, first half done: the candidate list for isolating argparse, read from codon-baseline.json and each module's imports (script w1414_candidates.py in the nemik scratch directory; the closure check is by import, not yet by probe compile). 18 modules fail in the stripped mode on argparse as their first error: ask_cli, blocks_cli, calwrite, critical, exportcli, floorasks, hostroot_cli, importer, metrics, pacing, pdf, pendingdeliver, pins, serve, starved, staticserve, waitemit, work. For each the question is whether argparse is the ONLY blocker in its import closure: the answer from the imports is NO for all 18. Seventeen import at least one other module Codon lacks or a nemik module that itself fails: work imports subprocess (and ask_cli imports work); pdf imports nothing failing among nemik modules and nothing else in the lacking set but argparse, yet it imports playwright, which is outside this check and would be the next first error; pins imports subprocess and tomllib and check; pacing, starved import rdflib, tomllib, importlib.resources, blocks and check; floorasks imports check (which fails); pendingdeliver imports witnesses (fails); exportcli imports check and withheld. The stdlib modules the baseline shows Codon lacks: argparse, collections.abc, contextlib, hashlib, http.client, importlib.metadata, importlib.resources, shlex, subprocess, tomllib, weakref, xml.etree.ElementTree, plus the third-party rdflib and pyshacl. CONSEQUENCE: moving main and the argparse import into a *_cli module changes a module's first error (for pacing, from argparse to rdflib or tomllib) but cannot make any of the 18 compile, so it lowers the codon entry count by 0; the count falls only when a module and its whole closure compile. The cheapest real fall is therefore a LEAF module whose only blocker is one of those stdlib modules and which nothing else blocks it: candidates to read next are the modules whose stripped error is collections.abc, contextlib or shlex alone and which import no rdflib: they do not need an argparse split at all. Whether the census treats a changed first error as better or worse is not defined (regressions() compares only compiles-versus-fails), so a split that moves argparse to rdflib passes the ratchet and gains nothing. Not probe-compiled; the 400 s census run is the proof and I have not spent it.

waypoints.next_bounded_step: Read the apply path in src/nemik/witnesses.py (where a witnessed card is marked done) and match ready_wake's line format ('<repo>:W<n> <old status> -> <new status>'); add the flip line on apply with a test; no new command, so none of the five registries; the queue-event source itself is mtools:W2247 (luthen-observability W1931)
waypoints.evidence: 2026-11-05T13:52:24Z: 2026-11-05 luthen-observability agreed (their W1931 note): the queue-event half is mtools' (mtools:W2247), the flip-line mode of nemik-witnesses --apply is nemik's. THEIR ONE REQUIREMENT: keep the flip line's format IDENTICAL to checks/ready_wake.py's one-line format, or tell them the difference, because their Monitor tails the current format. The format, read from ready_wake.changes(): a ready-count line is 'ready cards <old> -> <new>', and a peer-card line is '<repo>:W<n> <was> -> <now>' with a status word each side ('(not cited)' or '(no longer cited)' when the card enters or leaves the cited set); the status words are the queue's own (ready, working, blocked, done). So the flip line for a witnessed card closing is '<repo>:W<n> <old status> -> done'.

waypoints.title: Design the wake verdict gauge: read waitemit.py and wake.roster(), choose the series name and labels (wake required 0 or 1, the awake state), write the design on the card
waypoints.evidence: 2026-11-05T13:49:41Z: 2026-11-05 DESIGN (read src/nemik/waitemit.py, src/nemik/wake.py roster() and WakeRow; no code written). WHAT EXISTS: wake.roster(g, liveness, now, alarms) returns one WakeRow per workstream something waits on (inbound blocks, plus an owner whose alarm fired and who is not awake), each with repo, state (awake, asleep, idle or unknown, from luthen's loop_liveness verdict through AWAKE), last_tick, last_tick_age_s and a list of waiters; sleepers with waiters sort first. waitemit.py (the host job) already sends three gauges per pair of repos through mikemol.otlp (nemik_wait_oldest_ticks, nemik_wait_cards, nemik_wait_blocker_position; resource service nemik-waits, namespace nemik) with gauge_samples(edges, time_ns) -> Sample(name, value, time_ns, labels, unit). THE METRIC luthen asked for (W1928 option B: page on wake-required AND a stale stamp): nemik_wake_required{repo} = 1 when the workstream is on the roster with at least one waiter and its state is not awake, else 0; sent for EVERY known workstream (the union of the liveness keys and the queue repos), so a 0 is an explicit reading and a missing series means nemik did not run, not that nothing waits. A second gauge nemik_wake_waiters{repo} = the number of waiting cards (its row's waiting length, 0 when none), so a page can say how much is blocked. Labels: repo only (about ten values, low cardinality); the awake state is NOT a label (it changes the series identity as it flips); it is carried by the value of wake_required itself. WHERE: waitemit.py, beside the wait gauges, because it runs on the host where luthen's liveness is reachable (wake._checker_output runs luthen's checker) and metrics.py is served in the cluster where it is not; a new pure function wake_samples(rows, repos, time_ns) returns the Samples, emit() gets them from a roster built in main() from the same survey graph the edges come from. The 1/0 reading must not be taken from alarms alone: roster() puts an owner on the roster for a fired alarm, so a workstream with a fired alarm and no waiter reads 1 with waiters 1 (the alarm waits on itself), which is intended. REQUESTS: luthen's registry needs a metric_families row for each new name (W1604 carries the ask; luthen takes incident asks only while github:W90 is open, per github-14). CODON: waitemit is already in the codon baseline (argparse), so no change there. NEXT: W1604 builds wake_samples and wires it (waitemit.py, tests/test_waitemit.py), W1605 tells luthen-observability:W1928 the names.

standing: nemik repo rules (the fleet rules live in /home/mikemol/github/.claude/loop-prompt.md):
- Writer: /home/mikemol/github/nemik/.venv/bin/mikemol-paths-forward --state /home/mikemol/github/nemik/.claude/paths-forward.json. The queue goes only through it.
- No waivers: no noqa, no type: ignore; ruff, format and mypy ratchets must stay at or below baseline.
