- Push is deploy: a nemik push is a Flux ship (Forgejo build, deploy-state, namespace nemik). A stuck ship goes to luthen, never the operator.

- A new src/nemik module imported by the adapter or check breaks the relay, hooks and commands until bazel build //:.venv: build before wiring. The hook venv (.venv, a link to bazel-bin/.venv) holds symlinks into the working tree's src/nemik, so a staged edit is live to the hooks the moment it is written: a non-empty nemik-stale (it printed STALE say.py) is an order to run bazel build //:.venv before any further edit; after each staged edit to a file the hooks import (adapter, blocks, blocks_cli, check, history, metrics, rank, serve, wake) run nemik-inbound --help, nemik-check --help, nemik-rank --help and nemik-stale and write the four exit codes on the card; make staged edits to those files last in a round, so the tree is live-broken for the least time (nemik:R124 finding 1, file retro-r126.json, and nemik:R125 finding 1, file retro-r127.json: nemik-rank and nemik-inbound failed for about 11 min on 2026-11-01 after rank.py was wired to a module the venv had no link for).
- Cite a commit hash only after the command printed it, and check git log -1 is the intended subject.
- Never close a tick by --ledger, --render or --unlock while a --tick-close refusal stands: keep working.

- While the warm reviewer runs, close the tick with --reason "warm reviewer in flight: one token spender (reviewed-loop, github:W71; operator L107593 uuid d3b98176-043d-4c73-8689-048c2b566b87)" and send G0 and G1 right after, then idle until it returns; a close with that reason and no hand-back after it is a dodge. Use --tick-close --reviewing AGENT-ID once the pinned writer carries it (mtools:W2038).

- A duration quoted in a G1 carries both timestamps it was computed from, their difference and its kind (wall or CPU), or comes from a tool line that prints the elapsed time; never a figure estimated from memory (R7-F14).

- A dated G0 line is written on the card a stack advances BEFORE the first edit of the files that stack carries, and before the stack is submitted; the next G1 pairs three full stamps for each stack: the G0's, the earliest edit's and the submit's. The earliest edit is the stamp of the first Edit, Write, codemod or command tool call that touched the stack's files, read from the session transcript (mikemol-transcriptstruct --grep prints it as "at"); a file mtime is the last write and does not count. Remove this rule only when mtools:W2098 has landed with the same comparison (R9-F19, R11-F23, R12-F26). A defect found while other work is under way (a peer's report, a failing read) gets its card, with a manifest, and its G0 stamped before the first edit of the file it touches, even when the fix looks one line long: the card is minted first and the edit comes second (nemik:R179 finding 1, file retro-r179.json: W846, W1529 and W1536, each born mid-stack and each stamped after its edit, the lapse named in its own stamp and then repeated). The stamp comes first for EVERY edit, a docs-only edit included: there is no exemption, because the four lapses so far (W846, W1529, W1536 and W1580, the last a one-paragraph edit of docs/plc0415-cycles.md) were each a small edit that looked too small to need one; a lapse is named on the card and in the G1 (nemik:R208 finding 2, file retro-r208.json). The stamp is written with `.venv/bin/python3 tools/stampnote.py SYMBOL G0 TEXT`, which puts the UTC clock reading on the note itself (committed with tests/test_stampnote.py, nemik:W1568); a stamp written after an edit is labelled LATE in its own text, and the tool is to refuse or label it when `git status` shows a manifest path of the card already modified (nemik:R212 finding 1, file retro-r212.json: W1587's G0 was the fifth lapse; the check is not built, I still need to build it, W1568).

- A paydown card's G0 states N sites and K, the number of them whose fix was verified derivable BEFORE the G0 (a per-site decision from the tool's own output), candidates not yet verified are written as the range [0, K], and a premise about a tool cites the line of its definition that was read. The expectation is K, and a miss is judged against K, not N. For a batch of mechanical fixes the G0 also names the companion findings a fix can clear on the same line (EM102 clears TRY003, a TYPE_CHECKING move that removes a function-local import clears PLC0415) and the follow-on findings it can leave (I001, F401, ISC004, D202), and states the expected net as a range that counts both. A batch that applies fixes the tool labels unsafe names in its G0 the behaviour change the tool warns of and the check that covers it. An excess or a miss outside the range is attributed per file from the baseline diff in the same round (R9-F20, R10-F21, R13-F28, R14-F30, R15-F31, R16-C1). An axis a G0 has not measured is written "unmeasured", never as a range such as [0, 0]; the K probe of a src file is a copy placed inside the project beside it (src/nemik/probe_<name>.py, which the edit hook allows; only a copy from outside the project is refused), measured and deleted by exact path (nemik:R197 finding 1, file retro-r197.json: W1563's G0 wrote mypy [0, 0] for rank.py and the walrus rewrite raised it by 4). The codes a first ratchet write predictably raises are named in the G0 by edit kind and cleared before the write (nemik:R212 finding 3, file retro-r212.json): a rename to a public name carries a docstring (D103) with a Returns section (DOC201) and a Raises section when the body raises (DOC501), and ruff's own `--select I --fix` on every importer (I001); a new test file names its numbers (PLR2004) and gives read_text and open an encoding (PLW1514); a raise inside a try clause (TRY301, DOC501) and a try clause of more than five statements (PLW0717) are cut before the write by moving the call to a helper; a codemod that renames carries these in the same write, because the edit hook refuses an import and its use split across two edits. A G0 that quotes a pace read states the age in minutes at its own stamp, and a read over 10 minutes is re-run (`nemik-rank nemik --pace`) in the same step, before the stamp, not promised for before the submit: W1593's and W1596's G0s each said 're-read before submit' and the G1 could not confirm it (nemik:R213 finding 2, file retro-r213.json). A signature change that groups arguments into a record is probed on a probe copy BEFORE the G0 for the codes it raises, because W1626's audit took four codemod steps for what one probe would have shown: PLR0914 counts local variables EXCLUDING parameters but INCLUDING a parameter that is rebound (`x = x or ...` adds one), so unpacking the record into locals or rebinding it can push a function over 15; the pattern that worked is a record type that is a NamedTuple with defaults, a module constant for its all-default value used as the parameter default (`options: Rec = NO_REC`, no B008, no rebinding), and each option read as options.<name> in the body; the same record pattern cleared W1618 (Schedule), W1621 (Reading), W1622 (RankOptions) and W1626 (AuditOptions), and PLR0913 counts every parameter including keyword-only ones (nemik:R225 finding 2, file retro-r225.json). The ratchet's baseline is per FILE and per CODE: an edit that turns one code into another code the file does not already carry is REFUSED by the ratchet write even when the total falls (W1640: two PLC0415 in checks/claims.py became one E402, 'E402 1 > baseline 0'), so a G0 for a move or rewrite names the codes the new form raises and checks each against the file's baseline entry before the edit; the pace guard likewise refuses a stack that lowers none of the ratchets owed, so a mypy-only stack needs mypy to read behind at the submit, not only at the stamp (W1638, stack 998) (nemik:R230 finding 3, file retro-r230.json).

- Before a G1 is sent, --in-gate lists at least one stack, or the G1 says why none could be queued (nothing ready and mechanizable, with the check that shows it), the G1 gives every interval the gate sat empty as two full stamps, their difference and its kind (wall). The interval starts at the landing stamp from `TZ=UTC git reflog show --date=iso main`, read in UTC because the local zone repeats an hour when daylight time ends (nemik:R92 finding 1, file retro-r94.json: 01:43 -0400 and 01:16 -0500 on 2026-11-01), so every interval is two Z stamps (a commit's own date is the gate's begin time, not its landing) and ends at the next submit's stamp, a check that caused the wait is given with its own start and end stamps. The G1 also gives the stamp at which the previous reviewer round returned, and sets the in-gate stack's expected remaining time (from the recent gate wall times) against a review round plus the next stack's build and check time: where the gate would empty first, a second stack on files no queued stack carries is queued before the send, or the G1 says none exists and shows the check. After a reviewer return, the next stack's G0 is written before the first answer to a reviewer item, or the G1 says why an answer was a prerequisite, and the G1 gives the return stamp, that G0's stamp and the first answer's stamp (R11-F24, R12-F27, R14-F29, R16-F32). A turn never ends with a stack in the gate and no staged successor, unless the G1 names why none can be built and shows the check; staged means the real-file edit is made, mikemol-pycheck is read, the guards are run and the stack json is written, waiting only on a shared baseline (nemik:R101 finding 1, file retro-r103.json: the gate sat empty 13 min 21 s from 11:18:47Z to 11:32:08Z after a turn ended with no successor, and 72 min 51 s from 06:16:39Z to 07:29:30.6Z). A turn also never ENDS with the gate empty or with one stack in it and nothing queued behind: read --in-gate as the last act before closing a turn, and if it is empty or lists one stack with no queued successor, start the next probe and submit (the queue takes a successor behind a gating stack) or write on a card why none can be built, with the check (nemik:R136 finding 1, file retro-r138.json: the invariant held on eight landings from 02:19Z to 04:53Z and failed in four of the next five, the worst a 23 min gap that began when a turn ended four minutes after a landing with nothing queued). After a submit, the next 20 minutes of the turn belong to the successor, a stack of the OTHER baseline than the one in the gate (standing 16: a ruff stack cannot queue behind a ruff stack, nor a mypy stack behind a mypy stack): its scratch-copy measure and its G0 come before any reviewer answer, pace read for its own sake, card housekeeping or probe of something else, and the G1 gives the stamp of the successor's G0 against the predecessor's submit; the empty-gate cause was the same in R193, R195, R197, R199 and R201 (the successor was built after the landing instead of during the gate) and the diagnosis alone changed nothing (nemik:R201 finding 3, file retro-r201.json). The successor candidates are kept in a table on W1568 in the queue (lane, row, probed or not, measured K), updated at each landing and filled during gates, so the next stack's list is prepared before it is needed (nemik:R202 findings 1 and 2, file retro-r202.json). The gate's cost is set by WHICH files change, measured from the gate output of stacks 948 to 950 (2026-11-03): a stack that touches only tests and docs re-ran 6 of 465 test targets (bazel elapsed 65 s, the stack gated 8 min 53 s), a stack that touches ONE src/nemik module re-ran 462 of 465 (bazel elapsed 994 s and 824 s, 490 processes in linux-sandbox, the stacks gated 27 min 52 s and 24 min 29 s); so src edits are batched into one stack per gate and test-only or docs-only rows ride as extra entries, and a G1 gives the fresh-target count from the gate output line 'gate targets: N fresh of 465' (nemik:R208 finding 3, file retro-r208.json). The LONG LANE goes first: when one ratchet has far more landings to zero than the other (ruff 85 against mypy 9 on the pace read of 2026-11-04T01:25:47Z), session time goes to the long lane's probes and stacks first and the short lane's stacks are filler built while a long-lane stack gates (nemik:R209 finding 2, file retro-r209.json). An EMPTY gate is time-boxed: probe with a hard stop 30 minutes after the G0 stamp, and if K is not measured by then submit the smallest already-probed filler (nemik:R210 finding 1, file retro-r210.json). The landing step quotes the output line of `.venv/bin/python3 tools/working_unnamed.py` (never system python3) before the card is closed (nemik:R210 finding 2). The LANE CHECK comes before the build: read the pace, and build a mypy-only stack only when mypy is listed behind (the pace guard refuses a stack that lowers none of the ratchets owed); when only ruff and codon are owed, a mypy row rides as the SECOND entry of a ruff stack or queues behind a ruff stack in the gate, and the G0 quotes each lane's status from that read (nemik:R213 finding 1, file retro-r213.json: stack 960's first submit, W1590 alone, was refused). While mypy reads OK on the pace (not behind), the gate is serial in the ruff lane: a mypy-only stack is refused at submit and a ruff stack cannot queue behind a ruff stack, so the next ruff stack is probed, G0-stamped and built DURING the current gate, with its K measured and its tests run, and submitted the minute the predecessor lands; a mypy row rides as the SECOND entry of it, never alone (nemik:R215 finding 1, file retro-r215.json: the gate was empty about 6 minutes at each of two landings from 07:13Z to 07:58Z). The SHAPE of a stack is a ruff entry first, then the mypy bundle: a mypy-only stack is refused at submit once the bundle itself brings the mypy lane to ok (stack 981: the lane read behind at the BUILD stamp and ok with the bundle in the tree), so the first entry lowers ruff or codon, the following entries carry the mypy rows, and the lanes are re-read (the BUILD stamp's own tool read, or one more `nemik-rank nemik --pace`) just before the submit, not trusted from the stamp; keep a short list of ruff first-entry rows on W1568, each marked probed or unprobed, so the first entry is never the thing being hunted at the moment a bundle is ready (nemik:R222 finding 1, file retro-r222.json).

- Before a submit, run directly (the venv python, PYTHONPATH=src:tests) the guards a gate refusal has cost this repo: tests/test_architecture.py, test_no_dict_spread.py, test_no_waivers.py, test_namespaces.py, test_nested.py, and the tests of each touched module; a stack that adds an import to metrics.py or serve.py also runs checks/claims.py hub-modules-depend-on-everything-below. A refusal by a guard that was not run is recorded on the card as a miss (nemik:R66 finding 5, file retro-r68.json, W1219). A change that HOISTS an import (a function-local import moved to module level, or a name moved to another module) changes where a test must patch it: before the submit, grep the tests for setattr or monkeypatch of the SOURCE module's attribute (`setattr(check, "survey"`, `"nemik.check.survey"`) for every name the change moves, and run EVERY test file that mentions each touched module, not only the files the change edits (nemik:R238 finding 2, file retro-r238.json: stack 1006's first gate failed //:test_rank_survey after 811 s because W1656 hoisted rank's survey import and the test still patched check.survey).

- Before a stack is chosen, run `nemik-rank nemik --pace` yourself as the tick's first command and quote its stamp: the tick-open hook line prints the pace as of the open and can be a round old (nemik:R95 finding 1, file retro-r97.json, fourth miss: W1353 was chosen ruff-only from the 07:25:26Z hook line while the 08:25:26Z pace already had ruff ok and mypy and codon owed, and the gate refused the submit). The stack's first entry lowers a baseline the newest pace lists as behind; a paydown G0 names that stamp and that baseline, and the K probe (a scratch copy edited and measured before the G0) is run for any mypy paydown so the range is not [K, N] (nemik:R95 finding 2, file retro-r97.json); for a probe of a src file the K probe also runs tests/test_architecture.py and tests/test_namespaces.py on the probe tree before the G0, because checks/claims.py pins the module set of serve.py and metrics.py and the per-file ratchet does not see it (nemik:R100 finding 1, file retro-r102.json: the serve.py hoist passed ruff and mypy as a probe and failed test_architecture as the real file). The pace quoted in a G0 is at most 10 minutes old at the G0's own stamp: a card prepared during a gate re-reads the pace (`nemik-rank nemik --pace`) before its G0 is stamped, and the G0 gives the stamp and its age in minutes; a read older than that is a miss, not a note (nemik:R183 finding 2, file retro-r183.json: R170, R176 and W1542's G0 at 2026-11-03T10:54:19Z citing the 10:25:18Z read).

- Successors alternate baselines (nemik:R166 finding 1, file retro-r168.json; hooks stackahead.unbuilt_on, mtools:W2078): mikemol-commit refuses a queued stack that shares a file with a stack ahead unless it carries that stack's exact blob, so two stacks that both lower ruff-baseline.json cannot wait together and --freeze-from does not help. Keep each stack to ONE baseline file; queue a successor behind a ruff stack only if it lowers mypy-baseline.json or codon-baseline.json and shares no source file with it, and name the next three successors by baseline, each with its card, in the G1. A ruff successor is built during the gate and submitted the minute the stack ahead lands. A working card outside the published round is refused at submit while a ready round card is left out of the working set (hooks round_check, W1942): name the round's authority file in the G0 and work or clear it.

- A card is marked working when its stack is SUBMITTED, and the landed cards' marks are cleared (done or ready) at the landing, before the next submit (nemik:R169 finding 3, nemik:R171 finding 1 and nemik:R175 finding 1; hooks round_wire.in_gate, round_check, W1942). Testable clause: before each submit, every card whose status is working is the waypoint of an entry in a live queued or gating stack (this submit's included); a working card no entry names is either given its own entry in that stack or has its mark cleared first. The submit's round check exempts only a card a live stack names, so a mark that names no live stack is refused whenever a ready round card is left out of the working set. Two refusals so far: stack 890's first resubmit for W1509's stale mark, and stack 900's first submit for W1530, a pin test that rode the stack without an entry of its own, both 2026-11-03. The clause is run, not remembered: tools/working_unnamed.py (committed with tests/test_working_unnamed.py, nemik:W1532) reads the working cards (the writer's --working-stale 0) and the live stacks (--in-gate --json) and prints each working card no stack names; run it at every landing and before every submit, and put its output in the G1 (nemik:R183 finding 1, file retro-r183.json: stack 911's first submit was refused for W1535 kept working after its slice landed, the third refusal of the kind, W1532).

- Provenance before attribution: before a symptom in a fleet consumer (the pace unit, a gauge, a peer's gate) is blamed on a nemik change, or a nemik change is said to have fixed it, compare the consumer's BUILD IDENTITY with the code that changed: the pin sha or install path it runs, and the first line of the artifact it produced (the pace file's `build` key), against the commit. nemik's own tree reaches only the followed install (hooks and by-hand runs), never a pinned unit, and a by-hand run of the tree is not the unit's run; reproduce read-only with the tree's code beside the published artifact and compare the two before naming a cause. A claim about what a consumer reads carries its evidence on the card (nemik:R242 finding 1, file retro-r242.json: the pace unit runs a pinned build, sha ec56d66 installed 2026-10-27, so the tree edits blamed and credited for four all-mtools-unknown episodes never reached it; a one-line header comparison would have shown it hours earlier).

findings.finding: The hoist's import-time question stays open because the instrument was wrong for the effect: wall time with a 90 ms noise floor cannot resolve a difference that may be a few milliseconds. Use deterministic measures, which have no noise: for each entry module and hook command, the number and the list of modules imported (sys.modules after importing it, in a fresh interpreter, on the parent tree and the new tree; the difference is exactly the set of modules the hoist adds to that command's import path), and the sum of per-module self times from -X importtime for the added modules only, taken as the minimum of many runs rather than a median. If the hook path's module set did not grow (the hook commands do not import serve or metrics), the answer is 'no cost to hooks' by construction and the question closes with a list; if it grew, the added modules and their minimum self times give the bound. Record the module-set difference on W1561.
